tip: Passive adds -il to the stem: gönderdi (sent) becomes gönderildi (was sent), with no doer named.
-den dolayı means because of, and needs the ablative -den first: gürültü becomes Gürültüden dolayı (because of the noise).
Causative -ir makes someone do the act: içti (drank) becomes içirdi (made take), and the taker goes dative, hastaya.
To report a thought, -dığını turns the verb into a noun object: anlamadığını söyledi = said that he did not understand it.
-madan önce means before doing something: kararmak (to darken) becomes kararmadan önce (before it got dark).
-mıştım is the past before the past: sıkıldım (I got bored) becomes sıkılmıştım (I had gotten bored) for an earlier state.
ceza yemek literally is to eat a fine, the normal way to say get fined: trafik cezası yedim = I got a traffic fine.
ilgilenmek (to tend, take care of) pairs with -yle: bahçe becomes bahçeyle ilgilendi (took care of the garden).
In a passive, the doer gets tarafından (by): annem tarafından hazırlandı = were prepared by my mother.
-dığında means when something happened: yağmak (to fall) becomes yağdığında (when it snowed).
Proper nouns split off case suffixes with an apostrophe: İstanbul'a (to Istanbul), never written Istanbula.
A specific, definite object takes the accusative -u: form becomes formu (the particular form) as the thing acted on.
unutmak takes a verb turned into a noun with -mayı: sulamak (to water) becomes sulamayı unuttum (I forgot to water).
Past unreal condition: -saydık sets the if, -irdik the result: çıksaydık ... yetişirdik = had we left, we would have caught it.
Written as its own word, da means also or too: sağlığını da ihmal etme = do not neglect your health either.
sen becomes sana in the dative, an irregular form (not sene): sana ... söyleyeceğim = I will tell you.
-erdik marks a repeated past habit: çizmek (to draw) becomes çizerdik (we used to draw).
